title: Asymmetry in the evolution of the male and female germlines
content:
by Carina F. Mugal, Marie Sémon

A new study in PLOS Biology shows that in Drosophila, patterns of molecular evolution differ between genes expressed during oogenesis and spermatogenesis. Their evolutionary framework provides a basis for better understanding the link between molecular evolution of reproductive organs and the speciation process. Reproductive organs are under strong selective pressure during evolution. This primer discusses a recent PLOS Biology manuscript that has revealed asymmetric evolutionary divergence in Drosophila reproductive organs, wherein meiotic cell types in the testis emerge as hotspots of rapid change and ovary cell types remain more conserved.
author: Carina F. Mugal
